expected_revision.description: Revision from an earlier read. The write is refused if another agent changed the file since then.

origin.description: Pivot point.

rotation.description: Degrees, applied Z·Y·X about the origin.

parent.description: Parent group UUID or name; null or omitted places the node at the root.

origin.description: Rotation pivot; defaults to the cube center.

box_uv.description: Defaults to the model's box_uv setting.

texture.description: Texture for every face.

uv.description: [u1, v1, u2, v2] in project-resolution units (every texture spans 0..resolution whatever its pixel size); values past the resolution tile when the texture's wrap_mode is repeat. Ignored for box-UV cubes.

texture.description: Texture for this face; null disables the face.

faces.description: Cubes only. Per-face UV, texture or rotation changes; unlisted faces are kept.

parent.description: Move under this group; null moves to the root.

source.description: PNG data URL.

material.description: Material (UUID or name) this texture belongs to.

channel.description: PBR channel inside the material; defaults to color.

wrap_mode.description: repeat tiles the image when face UVs exceed the texture.

render_mode.description: emissive makes the texture glow in Blockbench and bb-render (signs, light panels).

color_value.description: Uniform RGBA 0-255, used when no color texture is assigned.

mer_value.description: Uniform metalness, emissive, roughness 0-255, used when no MER texture is assigned.

source.description: New PNG data URL; replaces the image, embeds it (dropping any link to a PNG file and any layers) and keeps every face and material assignment.

width.description: Pixel width of the new source (required with source).

height.description: Pixel height of the new source (required with source).

material.description: Material UUID or name; null removes the texture from its material.

render_mode.description: emissive makes the texture glow in Blockbench and bb-render (signs, light panels).

targets.description: Cubes, meshes, or groups (every cube and mesh inside is assigned).

texture.description: null disables the faces.

faces.description: Cube faces; defaults to all six.

mesh_faces.description: Mesh face keys; defaults to every face of each mesh.

name.description: Usually animation.<model>.<action>.

value.description: Numbers or Molang strings. Rotation in degrees, 5.0 sign convention.

parent.description: Group UUID or name the locator follows; null or omitted places it at the root.

rotation.description: Degrees; orients effects that use local space.

bind_to_actor.description: Keep the emitter attached to the entity.

origin.description: Pivot and position; vertices are relative to it. Defaults to the parent group's origin (Blockbench bone rig), else [0, 0, 0].

rotation.description: Degrees, Euler ZYX about origin.

parent.description: Parent group UUID or name; null or omitted places the mesh at the root.

vertices.description: {key: [x, y, z]} keeping your keys, or an array of [x, y, z] (4-character keys are generated). Positions are relative to origin.
3 or 4 distinct vertices, by key or by index (index into the vertex list/array; for edit_mesh, into the mesh's current vertex keys in saved order). Blockbench meshes do not support n-gons.

uv.description: Per-vertex [u, v] in project-resolution units: an object by vertex key, or an array aligned with vertices. Omit for Blockbench Auto UV.

anyOf.description: Texture UUID, name, or index in textures[].

texture.description: Texture for this face; null disables it; omitted uses the element-wide texture.
Texture for every face that does not name one.

color.description: Marker color 0-9; Blockbench picks one at random when omitted.

name.description: Defaults to Blockbench's name: the shape id, or mesh for cuboid.

texture.description: Texture for every face.

Quads losing a vertex become triangles; faces left with fewer than 3 vertices are removed.
Vertices to transform; omit for all.

rotate.description: Degrees, Blockbench Euler order ZYX, about pivot.

faces.description: Faces over existing vertices; faces without uv get Blockbench Auto UV.
Face keys; vertices no remaining face uses are deleted too.
Face keys to invert (Blockbench invert_face); omit for all.

distance.description: Merge vertices closer than this (Blockbench setting vertex_merge_distance, default 0.1).

keys.description: Candidate vertices; omit for all.

in_center.description: Move each merged vertex to its group's center and average UVs.

distance.description: Extrusion length in model units (Blockbench extend).

even_extend.description: Keep wall thickness even at corners shared by two faces.

faces.description: Faces to split; omit for all.

faces.description: Face keys; omit for all faces.

tools.name: mcp__bbmodel__bbmodel_export_bedrock_geometry
tools.description: Compiles a .bbmodel to Minecraft Bedrock geometry (.geo.json) using the same conventions as Blockbench's Bedrock codec: mirrored X, flipped up/down UVs, bb_main for root cubes, and visible bounds. Only cubes are exported; other element types are listed in skipped. Returns the JSON inline when no output path is given.

file.description: Path to a .bbmodel file, absolute or relative to the first workspace root.

output.description: Output .json path inside the workspace; omit to return the geometry inline.

identifier.description: Geometry identifier; defaults to the model identifier or name.

tools.name: mcp__bbmodel__bbmodel_export_java_block
tools.description: Compiles a .bbmodel to a Minecraft Java Edition block/item model .json the way Blockbench's Java Block/Item codec does: format_version, textures map (#id → namespace:folder/name), elements with 16-scale UVs, rotation (single-axis angle/axis for older versions, x/y/z for 1.21.11+ and 26.3), cullface, tintindex, display, groups and ambientocclusion. Meshes and other non-cube elements are skipped and listed in notes. Returns the JSON inline when no output path is given.

file.description: Path to a .bbmodel file, absolute or relative to the first workspace root.

output.description: Output .json path inside the workspace (usually assets/<namespace>/models/block/<name>.json); omit to return the model inline.

version.description: Target java_block_version; defaults to the model's own, then 26.3.

export_groups.description: Write Blockbench's groups outliner export (default true, like Blockbench).

export_pivots.description: Write zero-angle rotation blocks for cubes with a pivot (Blockbench's java_export_pivots, default true).

tools.name: mcp__bbmodel__bbmodel_info
tools.description: Summarizes a .bbmodel file: format, version, resolution, node counts, world-space bounds and the current revision. Start here before editing.

file.description: Path to a .bbmodel file, absolute or relative to the first workspace root.

tools.name: mcp__bbmodel__bbmodel_render
tools.description: Renders a .bbmodel file to a PNG with bb-render (headless three.js WebGPU), without Blockbench. Returns the image and its path. Optionally poses the model at a time in an animation clip. Views are relative to the model's front (-Z). The first render on a machine downloads and installs the render engine's packages with npm (three, three-blockbench and Dawn, about 130 MB) into a per-user cache folder; later renders reuse them.

file.description: Path to a .bbmodel file, absolute or relative to the first workspace root.

preset.description: bb-render preset; icon is orthographic with a transparent background.

output.description: PNG path inside the workspace; defaults to a scratch file outside it.

overwrite.description: Allow output to replace an existing PNG.

clip.description: Animation clip name or index; renders the pose at time.

tools.name: mcp__bbmodel__bbmodel_validate
tools.description: Runs geometry gates on a .bbmodel file in its rest pose and reports every violation by node name. Gates: outliner (broken references, duplicate UUIDs), unlisted_nodes, degenerate (slivers, inverted cubes), block_limits (Java or Bedrock block size), floating (parts touching nothing in the main body), interpenetration (deep overlaps across groups), mirror (left/right parts that are not mirror images). self_test plants each gate's defect into a copy and confirms the gate catches it; a gate that does not discriminate on this model should not be trusted. GeckoLib rules run automatically for geckolib_model files.

file.description: Path to a .bbmodel file, absolute or relative to the first workspace root.

block_limits.description: Defaults to java_block for java_block models, bedrock_block for bedrock_block models, otherwise none.

free_elements.description: Element names allowed to float (deliberately detached parts).

asymmetric.description: Group or element names excluded from the mirror gate.

mirror_x.description: X of the symmetry plane; defaults to 8 for java_block and 0 otherwise.

material_key.description: Exempt overlapping parts that share this material key.

geckolib.description: Force GeckoLib rules on or off.

tools.name: mcp__bbmodel__blockbench_launch
tools.description: Starts the Blockbench desktop app, optionally opening a file from the workspace (.bbmodel, .json, .obj, .gltf, .glb or .png). If Blockbench is already running, the file opens as a new tab in that window. Set wait_for_mcp_ms to wait until the desktop Blockbench MCP plugin answers, before driving the app with that server. The app is found from --blockbench, $BLOCKBENCH_PATH, blockbench on PATH, or the standard install folders. On Linux it needs a display, and snap or flatpak builds may be unable to read folders outside your home.

file.description: File to open, absolute or relative to the first workspace root.

wait_for_mcp_ms.description: Wait up to this long for the desktop plugin's MCP endpoint to answer; 0 returns right after launching.

tools.name: mcp__blockbench__capture_app_screenshot
tools.description: Returns the image data of the Blockbench app.

max_size.description: Longest side of the returned image in pixels; larger images are scaled down proportionally. Omit for full size.

format.description: Encoding of the returned image: "png" (default, lossless), or the smaller "jpeg" (no transparency: transparent pixels become white) or "webp".

tools.name: mcp__blockbench__capture_screenshot
tools.description: Returns the rendered image of a view. Defaults to the user's active viewport ("active"); pass the ID of an offscreen view from create_offscreen_view to render without disturbing the user, or a viewport ID from list_views.

view.description: View to target: "active" for the viewport the user last interacted with, the ID of an offscreen view from create_offscreen_view, or a viewport ID from list_views.

max_size.description: Longest side of the returned image in pixels; larger images are scaled down proportionally. Omit for full size.

format.description: Encoding of the returned image: "png" (default, lossless), or the smaller "jpeg" (no transparency: transparent pixels become white) or "webp".

tools.name: mcp__blockbench__geckolib_export_animations
tools.description: Compiles the project's animations into GeckoLib animation-file JSON, including the easing and easingArgs the plugin writes, and optionally writes it to a path. The text is formatted like Blockbench's own export (its JSON indentation, minify and final-newline settings). Reports which host API compiled it, since only the plugin-patched route stamps geckolib_format_version. Set mode='dialog' to trigger the plugin's own animation export action instead.

mode.description: compile returns the file content without touching the UI. dialog triggers the GeckoLib plugin's own export action, which opens a native save dialog for the user to complete and updates the project's cached export path.

path.description: Absolute filesystem path to write the compiled content to. Requires Blockbench filesystem permission. Only used in compile mode. Fails if the file exists unless overwrite is true.

overwrite.description: Replace an existing file at path. Defaults to false so a re-export never silently replaces a reference file.

max_content_length.description: Maximum characters of content to return. Use 0 to omit the content and only report its size.

animation_ids.description: Animation UUIDs or names to include. Omit to export every animation in the project.

tools.name: mcp__blockbench__geckolib_validate_model
tools.description: Checks the GeckoLib project against rules derived from the plugin and the GeckoLib runtime: bone-name charset and duplicates, mod ID and object ID validity, armor template bones, texture size against the UV base, and (optionally) compiled animation loop values, easing names, easing arguments and lengths. Each finding carries a stable check ID. Passing does not prove in-game correctness.

include_animations.description: Also compile the project's animations and validate their loop values, easings and lengths.

file per project). They keep their own mod ids (`dndsheets_dungeon`, `dndsheets_species`). Curios, Patchouli,

content.text:
El dragón ya tiene modelo propio con GeckoLib 4. No lo he visto en pantalla ni en el juego, y los otros 13 arquetipos del plan siguen sin hacer.

**Verificación**
- `./gradlew build` pasa con todos los chequeos, incluido `testJsonContent`.
- No pude ver nada: el viewport 3D sale en blanco tanto en el render headless como en Blockbench de escritorio. Solo vi la textura pintada en el panel UV.
- `runGameTestServer` no arranca en este entorno. Falla antes de cargar porque faltan Patchouli, Jade, Curios, Pehkui y Origins, que `mods.toml` ya exigía antes de mis cambios. Dejé escrito un test (`aShippedDragonWearsItsOwnModel`) que cubre el spawn, la textura, el tamaño bebé y el guardado/recarga NBT, pero no se ha ejecutado.

**Qué hay**
- **Entidad genérica `dndsheets:monster_model`:** un solo tipo de entidad que viste el arquetipo elegido por `appearance.model` y `appearance.variant` en `monsters.json`. Usa `baseEntity: "dndsheets:monster_model"`, así que un skin pack de otro mod de criaturas sigue ganando. Añadir un arquetipo son tres archivos de recursos y una línea de JSON, sin Java nuevo.
- **Dragón:** 51 cubos, 15 bones y 10 texturas de color (red, blue, green, black, white, brass, bronze, copper, gold, silver). Animaciones `idle`, `fly`, `attack`, `hurt` y `death`. Lo usan 40 dragones del bestiario y las crías se dibujan a mitad de tamaño. Ninguno de los 40 tiene `flies: true`, así que hoy ninguno usa `fly`.
- **Dependencia y tests:** GeckoLib 4.4.9 es ahora obligatoria en `build.gradle` y `mods.toml`. El self-test comprueba que cada modelo referenciado tenga su geometría, animaciones y textura.
- **Arte y licencias:** todo el arte sale de scripts propios en `tools/blockbench/mobs/`. No usé nada de otros mods ni de packs CC0. Dejé la política de licencias en `CREDITS.md`, `PROJECT_CONTEXT.md` y `CHANGELOG.md`.

**Qué falta**
- **Animación de ataque:** `MonsterModelEntity.play(entity, "attack")` existe, pero no lo llamé desde `MonsterActionManager`. Hasta entonces solo se anima el golpe recibido.
- **Signos de rotación:** las rotaciones de las animaciones (aleteo, mordida) usan los signos de Blockbench. Si salen invertidas se corrigen en `dragon.py`.
- **Auditoría de licencias:** no leí los `LICENSE` de los repositorios de los mods de criaturas. Solo los usé como referencia de diseño.

Antes de hacer los otros 13 arquetipos, ejecuta `./gradlew runClient` y spawnea un dragón desde `MonsterSpawnListScreen`. Dime cómo se ve (proporciones, textura, aleteo, tamaño de las crías) y lo ajusto. Después sigo con el resto en el orden del plan.

**Qué cambia en la práctica**
- **Colores y hex:** un color nuevo es una entrada en `variants.json`. `appearance.variant` también acepta un hex directo como `"#2a9d8f"`, y de ese color se derivan las demás tonalidades.
- **Archivos por arquetipo:** pasa de 10 PNG a 2 archivos (`mask.png` y `variants.json`), sin importar cuántos colores tenga. Los otros 13 arquetipos seguirán el mismo esquema.

   - **Item models.** The user added Blockbench (MCP + studio) and wanted 3D models for the mod's items, with design references from magic/RPG mods. Chosen scope: "Físicos clave". Chosen style: dark arcane fantasy (leather, brass, gems; matches DESIGN.md).
   - **Plugins and in-game check.** The user listed the installed Blockbench plugins (GeckoLib Models & Animations, Bone View, Animation Sliders, Animation to JSON Converter, Free Rotation, MCP Server). The new models did not show in game; the cause was stale build resources.
   - **Rest of the items and generic weapons.** "Crear modelos para el resto de objetos del mod y genericos para asignar a las armas".
   - **Mobs.** "Hacen falta modelos para los mobs y enemigos". User choices: GeckoLib + own entities; about 12–15 reusable archetypes.
   - The user rejected the first mob plan, asking: "Validar contra mods populares de criaturas, estrategias utilizadas para manejo de multiples modelos y diseños y considerar usar arte de licencia libre". The revised plan was approved. Its art policy: CC0, or CC-BY with credit; no copying other mods' art; original procedural art.
   - **Latest request** (with a screenshot of the dragons in game): "se ve bien, optimizar variantes y colores para no generar un modelo para cada una de ellas".

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - Minecraft 1.20.1, Forge 47.4.22, Parchment mappings, Java 17.
   - The mod has a single item, `dndsheets:token`. Each look (`ItemLook`) is a `CustomModelData` value of `ordinal()+1`; the enum is append-only.
   - Weapons are vanilla items carrying a `customModelData` from `weapons.json`. The overrides live in `assets/minecraft/models/item/<base>.json`.
   - GeckoLib 4.4.9 (cloudsmith maven), now a hard dependency, `[4.4,5)`.
   - One generic entity, `dndsheets:monster_model` (`MonsterModelEntity`), with synced `model`/`variant`/flying/baby data.
   - Monsters opt in with `baseEntity: "dndsheets:monster_model"` plus `appearance.model` and `appearance.variant`. A skin pack for another creature mod (`MonsterSkins` / `reskin`) still wins because it replaces `baseEntity`.
   - Each archetype ships one `mask.png` plus `variants.json` (palettes). The client colours the mask into a cached `DynamicTexture` per variant. `appearance.variant` may also be `"#RRGGBB"`, from which a palette is derived.
   - Mask encoding: R = mix toward dark, G = role×40 (roles: base, dark, belly, horn, membrane, eye), B = whiten, A = 255 painted.
   - Pipeline: the headless bbmodel MCP is driven through `tools/blockbench/bbmcp.py` (`Client().call(tool, args)`).
     - Its workspace root is `tools/blockbench`, so exports must go inside it and are then copied into the assets.
     - Box-UV shelf packing is done by the script, with a procedural painter.
     - Format is `geckolib_model`, exported with `bbmodel_export_bedrock_geometry` (format 1.12.0).
   - Animation JSON uses plain keys `idle fly attack hurt death`.
   - Wyrmlings keep `appearance.baby: true`, rendered at half size via `scaleModelForRender` and `getDimensions` scaled 0.5.

3. Files and Code Sections:

   **Item models (done earlier)**
   - `tools/blockbench/build_items.py`
     - Builds `dm_wand`, `move_wand`, `rest_kit`, `summon_card`, `summon_card_filled` with a swatch palette.
     - Defines `GENERATED_DISPLAY`, `pal()`, `palette()`, `rgb()`.
   - `tools/blockbench/build_more.py`
     - 16 ability medallions (glyph bitmaps).
     - 21 weapon models in `models/item/weapon/<id>.json`, sharing the texture `weapon_3d.png`. Their `customModelData` values are 1001–1021.
   - `src/main/resources/dndsheets/defaults/weapons.json`: `customModelData` added to those 21 weapons.
   - `assets/minecraft/models/item/*.json`: 16 vanilla override files. `stick` (used by flail) uses `handheld_rod`.
   - `tools/generate_item_icons.py`: `HAND_AUTHORED = set(LOOKS)`, so it no longer overwrites any look.
   - Weapons with a trident or fishing_rod base (javelin, spear, pike, trident, whip) were skipped.

   **GeckoLib setup**
   - `build.gradle`:
     - Repo: `maven { url = "https://dl.cloudsmith.io/public/geckolib3/geckolib/maven/"; content { includeGroup "software.bernie.geckolib" } }`
     - Dependency: `implementation fg.deobf("software.bernie.geckolib:geckolib-forge-1.20.1:4.4.9")`
   - `src/main/resources/META-INF/mods.toml`: geckolib dependency block placed after the pehkui block (mandatory, `[4.4,5)`, AFTER, BOTH).

   **Entity and rendering**
   - `src/main/java/net/hawthorn/dndsheets/entity/MonsterModelEntity.java` (new)
     - Extends `PathfinderMob`, implements `GeoEntity`.
     - Synced `MODEL`, `VARIANT`, `FLYING`, `BABY`. Defaults: `"dragon"` / `"red"`.
     - `configure(model, variant, flying)`; overrides `isBaby`/`setBaby` (calls `refreshDimensions`) and `getDimensions` (×0.5 for baby).
     - NBT keys: `Model`, `Variant`, `FlyingPose`, `Baby`.
     - Static `play(Entity, trigger)` calls `triggerAnim("action", trigger)` on the server; `hurt()` triggers `"hurt"`.
     - Controllers:
       - `"main"`: `death` (`thenPlayAndHold`), else `fly` or `idle` (`thenLoop`).
       - `"action"`: triggerable `attack` and `hurt`.
     - `createAttributes()`: max health 20, speed 0.25.
   - `src/main/java/net/hawthorn/dndsheets/init/DndsheetsModEntities.java` (new)
     - DeferredRegister `MONSTER_MODEL`: `MobCategory.MISC`, sized 1×1, tracking range 10.
     - `registerAttributes(EntityAttributeCreationEvent)`.
   - `DndsheetsMod.java`: registers `DndsheetsModEntities.REGISTRY` and adds the `registerAttributes` listener.
   - `src/main/java/net/hawthorn/dndsheets/client/MonsterModelRenderer.java` (new)
     - `@Mod.EventBusSubscriber(bus = MOD, value = CLIENT)`; extends `GeoEntityRenderer`; shadow 0.6.
     - `getDeathMaxRotation` returns 0.
     - `scaleModelForRender` multiplies width and height by 0.5 when the entity is a baby.
     - `reloadTextures(RegisterClientReloadListenersEvent)` registers a `ResourceManagerReloadListener` that calls `MonsterTextures.clear()`.

       - `geo/entity/<model>.geo.json`
       - `animations/entity/<model>.animation.json`

     - `get(model, variant)` caches the result of `build()`.
     - `build()`:
       - reads the palette;
       - opens `textures/entity/<model>/mask.png` as a `NativeImage`;
       - colours each pixel with `colour(abgr, palette)`;
       - registers a `DynamicTexture` at `dndsheets:dynamic/<model>/<sanitized variant>`.
       - On any exception it logs a warning and returns `MissingTextureAtlasSprite.getLocation()`.
     - `palette()`: a `#hex` variant calls `derived()`; otherwise it reads `variants.json` and falls back to the first key.
     - `clear()` releases the cached textures.
     - The unused `JsonElement` import and the `mix(float, …)` overload were removed.

   **Monster data and registry**
   - `MonsterRegistry.java`
     - `Appearance` record gained `String model, String variant`; `DEFAULT` and `GLOWING` are updated; `isDefault` checks both new fields.
     - `parseAppearance` reads `model` and `variant`; `writeAppearance` writes them.
     - `applyLooks` calls `own.configure(look.model, look.variant, block.flies())` before the early return.
     - The baby branch now also handles `MonsterModelEntity own` with `own.setBaby(true)`.
   - `monsters.json`: 40 color dragons (wyrmling, young, adult, ancient) moved to `baseEntity` `dndsheets:monster_model` with `appearance {model: "dragon", variant: <color>}`. Wyrmlings keep `"baby": true`.

   **Tests**
   - `src/test/java/net/hawthorn/dndsheets/JsonContentSelfTest.java`:
     - The appearance key set now includes `model` and `variant`.
     - The namespace and vanilla-item checks skip `model` and `variant`.
     - New check: a monster that names a model must have `baseEntity` `monster_model`, and must ship the geo, animation, `mask.png` and `variants.json`.
     - New check: the variant is a key of `variants.json` or starts with `#`.
   - `gametest/CombatantGameTests.java`: added `aShippedDragonWearsItsOwnModel`. It covers spawn, model/variant, baby, `Combatant`, and the NBT round trip. It has not been run (see Problem Solving).

   **Mob tooling and assets**
   - `tools/blockbench/mobs/mobkit.py` (rewritten in the latest step)
     - `Cube`, `pack`, `pixels()` (returns role / dark / whiten per pixel), `mask_png`, `preview_png`.
     - `Archetype.build` writes the bbmodel with a preview texture of the first palette, then exports the geo to `tools/blockbench/out` and copies it into the assets.
     - `install_textures` deletes old PNGs, writes `mask.png`, and writes `variants.json` as `{variant: {role: [r, g, b]}}`.
     - `install_animations` and the `keys()` helper.
   - `tools/blockbench/mobs/dragon.py`
     - 15 bones (root, body, neck1/2, head, jaw, tail1–3, wing_l/r, four legs) and 51 cubes.
     - `pair()` mirrors left/right cubes onto a shared UV.
     - 10 palettes: red, blue, green, black, white, brass, bronze, copper, gold, silver.
     - Animations: idle, fly, attack, hurt, death.
   - Assets:
     - `assets/dndsheets/geo/entity/dragon.geo.json`
     - `assets/dndsheets/animations/entity/dragon.animation.json`
     - `assets/dndsheets/textures/entity/dragon/mask.png`
     - `assets/dndsheets/textures/entity/dragon/variants.json` (the 10 per-colour PNGs were removed)

   **Docs**
   - `CREDITS.md`: creature models section and the licence policy.
   - `CHANGELOG.md`: "Unreleased" entry.
   - `PROJECT_CONTEXT.md`:
     - Removed "own creature models" from the out-of-scope lines.
     - Added an "Own creature models (GeckoLib)" section, now updated to describe the mask + `variants.json` design and "Done and seen in game: dragon".

4. Errors and fixes:
   - **Headless renders blank.** All bbmodel renders were white, and so was the desktop Blockbench viewport (WebGL issue on this machine). Verification relied on validate, the build, and the user checking in game.
   - **Item models not showing in game.** The `build/resources` output was stale; running `./gradlew processResources` fixed it.
   - **Bash heredoc failures.** A heredoc with nested quoting failed with "unexpected EOF". Java files were then written with the Write tool, and edits went through scratchpad Python scripts.
   - **Broken patch in `mobkit.py`.** A `'\n'` escape inside a patch broke the file; fixed with `chr(10)`.
   - **Export outside the workspace.** The bbmodel export refused paths outside its root; now exports to `tools/blockbench/out` and copies the file.
   - **Self-test failures.**
     - `model` was treated as an item id; fixed by skipping `model` and `variant`.
     - "a dragon wyrmling should come out as a baby": baby was restored for wyrmlings and implemented on the entity.
   - **`runGameTestServer` fails** in dev because the mods required by the existing hard dependencies (Patchouli, Jade, Curios, Pehkui, Origins) are missing. This was already the case and has nothing to do with GeckoLib.
   - **First mob plan rejected** by the user, who asked for validation against popular creature mods and consideration of free-licence art. The plan was revised with research on Ice and Fire variants, GeckoLib `getTextureLocation` variants, licences, and CC0 Quaternius / OpenGameArt packs.

5. Problem Solving:
   - `./gradlew build` passes with all checks, including `testJsonContent`, `checkPortabilityCoupling` and `checkAssetCredits`, after the mask/palette change.
   - The user confirmed the dragons render well in game.

   - "[Image #1] se ve bien, optimizar variantes y colores para no generar un modelo para cada una de ellas"

7. Pending Tasks:
   - The remaining 13 archetypes from the approved plan: goblinoid, brute, reptilian, demon, ooze, spider, beast, golem, elemental, bird, humanoid, undead, aquatic. Each is one mask, a palettes file, and a `monsters.json` mapping.

   - Phase 0 licence audit (LICENSE files of the reference mods); `reference/` notes.

# Plan: modelos propios para mobs y enemigos (GeckoLib)

## Context
Hoy los 330 monstruos de `monsters.json` son entidades vanilla (56 tipos distintos) con nombre, equipo (`appearance`) y escala Pehkui; el mod no registra ninguna entidad ni renderer (`MonsterRegistry.spawnAt` hace `type.create(level)` sobre `baseEntity`). Resultado: 52 dragones son el mismo ravager, goblins/orcos/kobolds son zombies, etc. `PROJECT_CONTEXT.md` (~l.706, 870, 922) marcaba "modelos propios de criaturas" como fuera de alcance hasta una decisión explícita: el usuario la tomó ahora.

Decisiones del usuario: **GeckoLib + entidades propias**, y cubrir **~12-15 arquetipos reutilizables** (cada uno con variantes de textura y escala), no 330 modelos. Arte original (el mod no puede redistribuir arte ajeno), hecho con Blockbench MCP.

## Diseño
- **Una sola entidad genérica** `dndsheets:monster_model` (`PathfinderMob` + `GeoEntity`) con dos datos sincronizados (`SynchedEntityData`): `model` (arquetipo) y `variant` (textura). Persisten en NBT. Un único `GeoEntityRenderer` + `GeoModel` resuelve rutas por esos dos campos:
  `geo/entity/<model>.geo.json`, `textures/entity/<model>/<variant>.png`, `animations/entity/<model>.animation.json`.
  Así añadir un arquetipo = 3 archivos + una línea en JSON, sin Java nuevo.
- **Cableado en datos**: nuevos campos opcionales en cada monstruo de `monsters.json`: `"model": "dragon"`, `"variant": "red"`. Si `model` existe, `MonsterRegistry.spawnAt` crea la entidad propia en vez de `baseEntity` (que queda como fallback si falta GeckoLib o el modelo). Escala por `size` con el `PehkuiCompat` existente; el resto de `spawnAt/applyLooks/tagAsMonster` (setNoAi, nombre, NBT `dndsheets`, turnos) se reutiliza tal cual.
- **Precedencia con skins de otros mods** (`MonsterSkins` / `reskin`): si un pack de skins aplica (mod de criaturas instalado) gana sobre el modelo propio, porque el usuario lo instaló a propósito; el modelo propio es el valor por defecto.
- **Animaciones**: `idle`, `walk` (solo si tiene IA), `attack`, `hurt`, `death`, `fly` para `flies:true`. Se disparan con `triggerAnim` desde el punto del servidor donde ya se anuncia ataque/daño/muerte (`MonsterActionManager` / `CombatManager`); sin lógica de combate nueva.
- **Dependencia**: GeckoLib 4 para 1.20.1 en `build.gradle` y `mods.toml` como dependencia obligatoria (verificar coordenada Maven y versión al implementar). Alternativa descartada: soft-dependency, por complicar el registro de la entidad.

## Validación contra mods de criaturas y estrategias de multi-modelo
Resultado de la investigación (fuentes abajo): la convención dominante es **un modelo por especie + variantes por textura**, elegidas desde datos de la entidad. Ice and Fire usa un modelo por tipo de dragón y texturas por variante/etapa/sexo con nombres tipo `red_1`…`red_5` y carpetas por elemento; sus addons añaden capas (emisivas, color por parte) sin tocar el modelo. GeckoLib 4 lo soporta directo: el `GeoModel` recibe la entidad en `getTextureLocation`, así que la textura sale de un campo sincronizado. Nuestro diseño (una entidad genérica con `model` + `variant`) sigue esa convención y se refuerza con:
- Etapa de crecimiento (wyrmling/joven/adulto/antiguo) = **escala**, no modelo nuevo (ya hay `size` + Pehkui).
- Capa **emisiva** opcional por variante (`<variant>_glow.png`, GeckoLib `AutoGlowingGeoLayer`) para ojos, aliento, ascuas, runas.
- Convención de rutas fija: `textures/entity/<model>/<variant>.png`; añadir un color = un PNG y una línea de JSON.
- Compatibilidad con mods de criaturas: los skin packs existentes (`MonsterSkins`) ya cubren Ice and Fire, Alex's Mobs, Mowzie's, Cataclysm, etc.; el modelo propio es el valor por defecto cuando no están. No se compite con ellos ni se copia su arte.
- Atención a la versión: el plugin "GeckoLib Models" de Blockbench debe exportar formato GeckoLib 4 (hay reportes de fallos al mezclar modelos de GeckoLib 5 con proyectos 4.x).

## Licencias y arte libre
- **No copiar ni convertir arte de mods de criaturas.** Los alojamientos citan GPL-3.0 para Alex's Mobs, pero eso parece cubrir el código y no queda claro para modelos/texturas; Mowzie's Mobs y Cataclysm no muestran licencia verificable. Se usan solo como **referencia de diseño** (siluetas, proporciones, paletas), y antes de tocar nada de ellos habría que leer el LICENSE del repositorio oficial.
- **Política de arte**: solo **CC0** (sin atribución obligatoria) y, si hace falta, **CC-BY** con crédito en un `CREDITS.md`. Excluidos CC-BY-SA (copyleft), NC y "todos los derechos reservados".
- **Fuentes libres candidatas** (verificar licencia en la página original antes de usar): Quaternius *Lowpoly Animated Monsters* (CC0; incluye dragón, murciélago, esqueleto, slime), Quaternius *Ultimate Monsters* (50 monstruos; la ficha de Sketchfab es contradictoria entre CC0 y CC-BY, confirmar en quaternius.com), OpenGameArt *Voxel creature pack1* (CC0; dragón verde y demonio, formato MagicaVoxel) y *Cute Animated Monsters* (CC0). El goblin de OpenGameArt es CC-BY-SA: descartado.
- **Uso práctico**: son mallas poligonales/voxel, no cubos de Minecraft. Se usan como **referencia de proporciones** (y los voxel como base para reconstruir en cubos); los modelos finales de cubos y las texturas se rehacen en Blockbench, así el resultado es obra propia coherente con la regla actual de `ItemLook` ("arte original"). Si se importa algo literal, se registra en `CREDITS.md`.
- Comprobar la licencia del propio mod (`LICENSE` del repo) para que sea compatible con CC0/CC-BY.

## Arquetipos (14) y qué monstruos cubren
Agrupación según `baseEntity` actual: dragon (los 52 ravager: 10 colores × wyrmling/joven/adulto/antiguo por escala), goblinoid (goblin, hobgoblin, bugbear), brute (orco, ogro, troll), reptilian (kobold, lizardfolk, serpientes/cocodrilos), demon (diablos, demonios, balor/pit fiend), ooze (slimes/oozes), spider, beast (lobos, felinos, osos), golem (golems y gigantes), elemental (mephits, imp, fuego/aire), bird (águilas, grifos, harpías), humanoid_basic (bandido, cultista, guardia con `appearance`), undead (esqueleto/zombi/momia), aquatic (tiburón, kraken, aboleth). El detalle exacto de cada mapeo se fija al implementar leyendo `monsters.json`; los que no encajan siguen con su entidad vanilla.

## Fases
0. **Auditoría de licencias y tablero de referencias**: leer los LICENSE de los repos de los mods usados como referencia y las páginas de los packs CC0; crear `CREDITS.md` y una carpeta `tools/blockbench/mobs/reference/` (notas y enlaces, sin binarios de terceros) con silueta y paleta objetivo por arquetipo.
1. **Vertical slice con el dragón**: dependencia, entidad + renderer genérico, atributos (`EntityAttributeCreationEvent`), `spawnAt` con `model/variant`, 1 modelo `dragon` con textura roja y animaciones idle/fly/attack/death. Probar `/dnd`-spawn en `runClient` (vuelo, escala, guardado/recarga, turnos, daño).
2. **Resto de arquetipos**, un script por modelo (extender `tools/blockbench/`, patrón `build_items.py`: cubos + paleta → `.bbmodel` de formato `geckolib_model` → export Bedrock geometry vía `bbmodel_export_bedrock_geometry` → instalar en `assets/dndsheets/geo/entity/`). Animaciones generadas como JSON de GeckoLib por script (el MCP headless no exporta animaciones GeckoLib; alternativa: Blockbench de escritorio con el plugin "animation to JSON").

<system-reminder>

Plan contents:

# Plan: modelos propios para mobs y enemigos (GeckoLib)

## Context
Hoy los 330 monstruos de `monsters.json` son entidades vanilla (56 tipos distintos) con nombre, equipo (`appearance`) y escala Pehkui; el mod no registra ninguna entidad ni renderer (`MonsterRegistry.spawnAt` hace `type.create(level)` sobre `baseEntity`). Resultado: 52 dragones son el mismo ravager, goblins/orcos/kobolds son zombies, etc. `PROJECT_CONTEXT.md` (~l.706, 870, 922) marcaba "modelos propios de criaturas" como fuera de alcance hasta una decisión explícita: el usuario la tomó ahora.

Decisiones del usuario: **GeckoLib + entidades propias**, y cubrir **~12-15 arquetipos reutilizables** (cada uno con variantes de textura y escala), no 330 modelos. Arte original (el mod no puede redistribuir arte ajeno), hecho con Blockbench MCP.

## Diseño
- **Una sola entidad genérica** `dndsheets:monster_model` (`PathfinderMob` + `GeoEntity`) con dos datos sincronizados (`SynchedEntityData`): `model` (arquetipo) y `variant` (textura). Persisten en NBT. Un único `GeoEntityRenderer` + `GeoModel` resuelve rutas por esos dos campos:
  `geo/entity/<model>.geo.json`, `textures/entity/<model>/<variant>.png`, `animations/entity/<model>.animation.json`.
  Así añadir un arquetipo = 3 archivos + una línea en JSON, sin Java nuevo.
- **Cableado en datos**: nuevos campos opcionales en cada monstruo de `monsters.json`: `"model": "dragon"`, `"variant": "red"`. Si `model` existe, `MonsterRegistry.spawnAt` crea la entidad propia en vez de `baseEntity` (que queda como fallback si falta GeckoLib o el modelo). Escala por `size` con el `PehkuiCompat` existente; el resto de `spawnAt/applyLooks/tagAsMonster` (setNoAi, nombre, NBT `dndsheets`, turnos) se reutiliza tal cual.
- **Precedencia con skins de otros mods** (`MonsterSkins` / `reskin`): si un pack de skins aplica (mod de criaturas instalado) gana sobre el modelo propio, porque el usuario lo instaló a propósito; el modelo propio es el valor por defecto.
- **Animaciones**: `idle`, `walk` (solo si tiene IA), `attack`, `hurt`, `death`, `fly` para `flies:true`. Se disparan con `triggerAnim` desde el punto del servidor donde ya se anuncia ataque/daño/muerte (`MonsterActionManager` / `CombatManager`); sin lógica de combate nueva.
- **Dependencia**: GeckoLib 4 para 1.20.1 en `build.gradle` y `mods.toml` como dependencia obligatoria (verificar coordenada Maven y versión al implementar). Alternativa descartada: soft-dependency, por complicar el registro de la entidad.

## Validación contra mods de criaturas y estrategias de multi-modelo
Resultado de la investigación (fuentes abajo): la convención dominante es **un modelo por especie + variantes por textura**, elegidas desde datos de la entidad. Ice and Fire usa un modelo por tipo de dragón y texturas por variante/etapa/sexo con nombres tipo `red_1`…`red_5` y carpetas por elemento; sus addons añaden capas (emisivas, color por parte) sin tocar el modelo. GeckoLib 4 lo soporta directo: el `GeoModel` recibe la entidad en `getTextureLocation`, así que la textura sale de un campo sincronizado. Nuestro diseño (una entidad genérica con `model` + `variant`) sigue esa convención y se refuerza con:
- Etapa de crecimiento (wyrmling/joven/adulto/antiguo) = **escala**, no modelo nuevo (ya hay `size` + Pehkui).
- Capa **emisiva** opcional por variante (`<variant>_glow.png`, GeckoLib `AutoGlowingGeoLayer`) para ojos, aliento, ascuas, runas.
- Convención de rutas fija: `textures/entity/<model>/<variant>.png`; añadir un color = un PNG y una línea de JSON.
- Compatibilidad con mods de criaturas: los skin packs existentes (`MonsterSkins`) ya cubren Ice and Fire, Alex's Mobs, Mowzie's, Cataclysm, etc.; el modelo propio es el valor por defecto cuando no están. No se compite con ellos ni se copia su arte.
- Atención a la versión: el plugin "GeckoLib Models" de Blockbench debe exportar formato GeckoLib 4 (hay reportes de fallos al mezclar modelos de GeckoLib 5 con proyectos 4.x).

## Licencias y arte libre
- **No copiar ni convertir arte de mods de criaturas.** Los alojamientos citan GPL-3.0 para Alex's Mobs, pero eso parece cubrir el código y no queda claro para modelos/texturas; Mowzie's Mobs y Cataclysm no muestran licencia verificable. Se usan solo como **referencia de diseño** (siluetas, proporciones, paletas), y antes de tocar nada de ellos habría que leer el LICENSE del repositorio oficial.
- **Política de arte**: solo **CC0** (sin atribución obligatoria) y, si hace falta, **CC-BY** con crédito en un `CREDITS.md`. Excluidos CC-BY-SA (copyleft), NC y "todos los derechos reservados".
- **Fuentes libres candidatas** (verificar licencia en la página original antes de usar): Quaternius *Lowpoly Animated Monsters* (CC0; incluye dragón, murciélago, esqueleto, slime), Quaternius *Ultimate Monsters* (50 monstruos; la ficha de Sketchfab es contradictoria entre CC0 y CC-BY, confirmar en quaternius.com), OpenGameArt *Voxel creature pack1* (CC0; dragón verde y demonio, formato MagicaVoxel) y *Cute Animated Monsters* (CC0). El goblin de OpenGameArt es CC-BY-SA: descartado.
- **Uso práctico**: son mallas poligonales/voxel, no cubos de Minecraft. Se usan como **referencia de proporciones** (y los voxel como base para reconstruir en cubos); los modelos finales de cubos y las texturas se rehacen en Blockbench, así el resultado es obra propia coherente con la regla actual de `ItemLook` ("arte original"). Si se importa algo literal, se registra en `CREDITS.md`.
- Comprobar la licencia del propio mod (`LICENSE` del repo) para que sea compatible con CC0/CC-BY.

## Arquetipos (14) y qué monstruos cubren
Agrupación según `baseEntity` actual: dragon (los 52 ravager: 10 colores × wyrmling/joven/adulto/antiguo por escala), goblinoid (goblin, hobgoblin, bugbear), brute (orco, ogro, troll), reptilian (kobold, lizardfolk, serpientes/cocodrilos), demon (diablos, demonios, balor/pit fiend), ooze (slimes/oozes), spider, beast (lobos, felinos, osos), golem (golems y gigantes), elemental (mephits, imp, fuego/aire), bird (águilas, grifos, harpías), humanoid_basic (bandido, cultista, guardia con `appearance`), undead (esqueleto/zombi/momia), aquatic (tiburón, kraken, aboleth). El detalle exacto de cada mapeo se fija al implementar leyendo `monsters.json`; los que no encajan siguen con su entidad vanilla.

## Fases
0. **Auditoría de licencias y tablero de referencias**: leer los LICENSE de los repos de los mods usados como referencia y las páginas de los packs CC0; crear `CREDITS.md` y una carpeta `tools/blockbench/mobs/reference/` (notas y enlaces, sin binarios de terceros) con silueta y paleta objetivo por arquetipo.
1. **Vertical slice con el dragón**: dependencia, entidad + renderer genérico, atributos (`EntityAttributeCreationEvent`), `spawnAt` con `model/variant`, 1 modelo `dragon` con textura roja y animaciones idle/fly/attack/death. Probar `/dnd`-spawn en `runClient` (vuelo, escala, guardado/recarga, turnos, daño).
2. **Resto de arquetipos**, un script por modelo (extender `tools/blockbench/`, patrón `build_items.py`: cubos + paleta → `.bbmodel` de formato `geckolib_model` → export Bedrock geometry vía `bbmodel_export_bedrock_geometry` → instalar en `assets/dndsheets/geo/entity/`). Animaciones generadas como JSON de GeckoLib por script (el MCP headless no exporta animaciones GeckoLib; alternativa: Blockbench de escritorio con el plugin "animation to JSON").
3. **Datos y documentación**: añadir `model/variant` a `monsters.json`, texturas por variante, `MonsterSkins` precedencia, actualizar `PROJECT_CONTEXT.md` (mover "modelos propios" de fuera de alcance a hecho, tabla arquetipo→monstruos) y `CHANGELOG.md`.

## Archivos críticos

- Nuevos: `init/DndsheetsModEntities.java`, `entity/MonsterModelEntity.java`, `client/MonsterModelRenderer.java` (+ `GeoModel`), registro de renderer/atributos en `DndsheetsMod`/`client`
- `MonsterRegistry.java` (`spawnAt`, `applyLooks`, esquema de parseo: campos `model`, `variant`), `MonsterSkins.java` (precedencia)

- Reutilizar: `PehkuiCompat` (escala), `MonsterRegistry.tagAsMonster`, patrón `CombatFx`/`ConditionBillboards` para efectos cliente.

## Riesgos
- Hitbox: `EntityDimensions` fijas por tipo; los dragones grandes dependen de Pehkui (ya usado) o de dimensiones por `size` en `getDimensions`.
- Los renders headless de bbmodel salen en blanco: revisar modelos con Blockbench de escritorio (`mcp__blockbench__capture_app_screenshot`) y en `runClient`.
- Mundos existentes: los monstruos ya spawneados siguen vanilla (no se migran); solo los nuevos usan el modelo.
- Primera vez que el mod depende de otra librería: confirmar compatibilidad con la versión de Forge 47.4.22.

## bbmodel
Edits and checks Blockbench .bbmodel files directly on disk, without the Blockbench app, so several agents can work in parallel. Workflow: bbmodel_create or bbmodel_info, then bbmodel_edit with batches of operations, then bbmodel_validate (and bbmodel_validate_animations) and bbmodel_contact_sheet to review. Every read returns a revision; pass it as expected_revision when writing so another agent's edits are never overwritten silently. Files open in Blockbench do not reload automatically; reopen them after headless edits, and do not edit the same file in both at once. Write results carry web_app links that open the model in the Blockbench web app (the file travels in the URL, nothing is uploaded): put web_app.url in your reply to the user, or geometry_url and launcher.file_url when the full URL is too long. bbmodel_web_url makes one for any file. Particle effects: bbmodel_particle_effect writes a Bedrock particle file from a preset or design knobs, bbmodel_edit add_locator and set_particle_keyframe place it on an animation, and bbmodel_particle_pack delivers the used effects to a resource pack. blockbench_launch starts the Blockbench desktop app with a file, or opens it in the running app.

## claude-in-chrome
**IMPORTANT: If the Chrome browser tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load them with ToolSearch before calling them, and batch every tool you expect to need into ONE ToolSearch call (the select query accepts a comma-separated list). Do NOT load tools one at a time; each separate ToolSearch call wastes a full round-trip.**

Start a browser task whose tools are not yet loaded with a single call loading the core set:

ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_close_mcp"

Add task-specific tools to the same call when the task obviously needs them: read_console_messages / read_network_requests for debugging, form_input for forms, gif_creator for recordings, javascript_tool for page scripting. Only issue a second ToolSearch if the task later needs a tool you did not anticipate.

## claude.ai Claude Docs
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>

<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>

# Ponytail

You are a lazy senior developer. Lazy means efficient, not careless. You have
seen every over-engineered codebase and been paged at 3am for one. The best
code is the code never written.

## Persistence

ACTIVE EVERY RESPONSE. No drift back to over-building. Still active if
unsure. Off only: "stop ponytail" / "normal mode". Default: **full**.
Switch: `/ponytail lite|full|ultra`.

## The ladder

Stop at the first rung that holds:

1. **Does this need to exist at all?** Speculative need = skip it, say so in one line. (YAGNI)
2. **Already in this codebase?** A helper, util, type, or pattern that already lives here → reuse it. Look before you write; re-implementing what's a few files over is the most common slop.
3. **Stdlib does it?** Use it.
4. **Native platform feature covers it?** `<input type="date">` over a picker lib, CSS over JS, DB constraint over app code.
5. **Already-installed dependency solves it?** Use it. Never add a new one for what a few lines can do.
6. **Can it be one line?** One line.
7. **Only then:** the minimum code that works.

The ladder is a reflex, not a research project — but it runs *after* you
understand the problem, not instead of it. Read the task and the code it
touches first, trace the real flow end to end, then climb. Two rungs work →
take the higher one and move on. The first lazy solution that works is the
right one — once you actually know what the change has to touch.

**Bug fix = root cause, not symptom.** A report names a symptom. Before you
edit, grep every caller of the function you're about to touch. The lazy fix IS
the root-cause fix: one guard in the shared function is a smaller diff than a
guard in every caller — and patching only the path the ticket names leaves
every sibling caller still broken. Fix it once, where all callers route through.

## Rules

- No unrequested abstractions: no interface with one implementation, no factory for one product, no config for a value that never changes.
- No boilerplate, no scaffolding "for later", later can scaffold for itself.
- Deletion over addition. Boring over clever, clever is what someone decodes at 3am.
- Fewest files possible. Shortest working diff wins — but only once you understand the problem. The smallest change in the wrong place isn't lazy, it's a second bug.
- Complex request? Ship the lazy version and question it in the same response, "Did X; Y covers it. Need full X? Say so." Never stall on an answer you can default.
- Two stdlib options, same size? Take the one that's correct on edge cases. Lazy means writing less code, not picking the flimsier algorithm.
- Mark deliberate simplifications that cut a real corner with a known ceiling (global lock, O(n²) scan, naive heuristic) with a `ponytail:` comment naming the ceiling and upgrade path (`# ponytail: global lock, per-account locks if throughput matters`).

## Output

Code first. Then at most three short lines: what was skipped, when to add it.
No essays, no feature tours, no design notes. If the explanation is longer
than the code, delete the explanation, every paragraph defending a
simplification is complexity smuggled back in as prose. Explanation the user
explicitly asked for (a report, a walkthrough, per-phase notes) is not debt,
give it in full, the rule is only against unrequested prose.

Pattern: `[code] → skipped: [X], add when [Y].`

## Intensity

| Level | What change |
|-------|------------|
| **full** | The ladder enforced. Stdlib and native first. Shortest diff, shortest explanation. Default. |

Example: "Add a cache for these API responses."
- full: "`@lru_cache(maxsize=1000)` on the fetch function. Skipped custom cache class, add when lru_cache measurably falls short."

## When NOT to be lazy

Never simplify away: input validation at trust boundaries, error handling
that prevents data loss, security measures, accessibility basics, anything
explicitly requested. User insists on the full version → build it, no
re-arguing.

Never lazy about understanding the problem. The ladder shortens the
solution, never the reading. Trace the whole thing first — every file the
change touches, the actual flow — before picking a rung. Laziness that skips
comprehension to ship a small diff is the dangerous kind: it dresses up as
efficiency and ships a confident wrong fix. Read fully, then be lazy.

Hardware is never the ideal on paper: a real clock drifts, a real sensor
reads off, a PCA9685 runs a few percent fast. Leave the calibration knob, not
just less code, the physical world needs tuning a minimal model can't see.

Lazy code without its check is unfinished. Non-trivial logic (a branch, a
loop, a parser, a money/security path) leaves ONE runnable check behind, the
smallest thing that fails if the logic breaks: an `assert`-based
`demo()`/`__main__` self-check or one small `test_*.py`. No frameworks, no
fixtures, no per-function suites unless asked. Trivial one-liners need no
test, YAGNI applies to tests too.

## Boundaries

Ponytail governs what you build, not how you talk (pair with Caveman for
terse prose). "stop ponytail" / "normal mode": revert. Level persists until
changed or session end.

The shortest path to done is the right path.

For example, use pattern: "[MyApp]" to filter for application-specific logs rather than reading all console output.

## Alerts and dialogs

IMPORTANT: Do not trigger JavaScript alerts, confirms, prompts, or browser modal dialogs through your actions. These browser dialogs block all further browser events and will prevent the extension from receiving any subsequent commands. Instead, when possible, use console.log for debugging and then use the mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_console_messages tool to read those log messages. If a page has dialog-triggering elements:
1. Avoid clicking buttons or links that may trigger alerts (e.g., "Delete" buttons with confirmation dialogs)
2. If you must interact with such elements, warn the user first that this may interrupt the session
3. Use mcp__claude-in-chrome__javascript_tool to check for and dismiss any existing dialogs before proceeding

If you accidentally trigger a dialog and lose responsiveness, inform the user they need to manually dismiss it in the browser.

## Avoid rabbit holes and loops

When using browser automation tools, stay focused on the specific task. If you encounter any of the following, stop and ask the user for guidance:
- Unexpected complexity or tangential browser exploration
- Browser tool calls failing or returning errors after 2-3 attempts
- No response from the browser extension
- Page elements not responding to clicks or input
- Pages not loading or timing out
- Unable to complete the browser task despite multiple approaches

Explain what you attempted, what went wrong, and ask how the user would like to proceed. Do not keep retrying the same failing browser action or explore unrelated pages without checking in first.

## Tab context and session startup

IMPORTANT: At the start of each browser automation session, call mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp first to get information about the user's current browser tabs. Use this context to understand what the user might want to work with before creating new tabs.

Never reuse tab IDs from a previous/other session. Follow these guidelines:
1. Only reuse an existing tab if the user explicitly asks to work with it
2. Otherwise, create a new tab with mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp
3. If a tool returns an error indicating the tab doesn't exist or is invalid, call tabs_context_mcp to get fresh tab IDs
4. When a tab is closed by the user or a navigation error occurs, call tabs_context_mcp to see what tabs are available

Write code that reads like the surrounding code: match its comment density, naming, and idiom.

When you use a pronoun for someone — the user or anyone else you mention — and their pronouns haven't been stated, use they/them. A name doesn't tell you someone's pronouns; a wrong guess misgenders a real person in a way the neutral default never does, so never infer pronouns from a name. This applies to all user-visible text, including visible thinking.

For actions that are hard to reverse or outward-facing, confirm first unless durably authorized or explicitly told to proceed without asking; approval in one context doesn't extend to the next. Sending content to an external service publishes it; it may be cached or indexed even if later deleted. Before deleting or overwriting, look at the target. Report outcomes faithfully: if tests fail, say so with the output; if a step was skipped, say that; when something is done and verified, state it plainly without hedging.

# Memory

After writing the file, add a one-line pointer in `MEMORY.md` (`- [Title](file.md) — hook`). `MEMORY.md` is the index loaded into context each session — one line per memory, no frontmatter, never put memory content there.
