tools.name: mcp__bbmodel__bbmodel_create
tools.description: Creates a new, empty .bbmodel file (format 5.0). Build it up with bbmodel_edit. Refuses to replace an existing file unless overwrite is true.

file.description: Path to a .bbmodel file, absolute or relative to the first workspace root.

format.description: Blockbench format ID: free, bedrock, bedrock_block, java_block, geckolib_model, modded_entity, ...

box_uv.description: Defaults to true for entity formats (bedrock, geckolib_model, modded_entity, ...) and false otherwise.

tools.name: mcp__bbmodel__bbmodel_edit
tools.description: Applies edit operations to a .bbmodel file in order, as one atomic write. If any operation fails, nothing is written and the error names the failing operation. Operations (field op): add_group {name, origin, rotation, parent}; add_cube {name, from, to, origin?, rotation?, inflate?, parent?, box_uv?, uv_offset?, mirror_uv?, texture?, faces?} (box-UV faces are laid out automatically); update_node {target, name?, origin?, rotation?, from?, to?, inflate?, uv_offset?, mirror_uv?, faces?, parent?} (parent moves the node; box UV is recomputed); remove_node {target} (groups are removed with their contents and animators); add_texture {name, source: PNG data URL, width, height, material?, channel?, wrap_mode?, render_mode?} (bbmodel_add_texture reads a PNG file for you); add_material {name, color_value?, mer_value?, subsurface_value?} (a PBR material; its textures fill the color, normal or height, and mer channels); update_material {target, name?, color_value?, mer_value?, subsurface_value?}; update_texture {target, name?, source?, width?, height?, material?, channel?, wrap_mode?, render_mode?} (material null removes it from its material); assign_texture {targets, texture, faces?, mesh_faces?} (cubes and meshes); add_animation {name, length, loop, snapping}; remove_animation {animation}; set_keyframe {animation, bone, channel, time, value, interpolation} (replaces a key at the same channel and time); remove_keyframe {animation, bone, channel, time}; set_model_properties {name?, model_identifier?, resolution?}; add_locator {name, parent?, position, rotation?, ignore_inherited_scale?} (a named point particle effects spawn at; position is absolute model units); set_particle_keyframe {animation, time, effect, file?, locator?, pre_effect_script?, bind_to_actor?} (file is the particle JSON path relative to the .bbmodel, from bbmodel_particle_effect; replaces the same effect at the same time); remove_particle_keyframe {animation, time, effect?}; add_mesh {name, vertices (key map or [x,y,z] list, relative to origin), faces [{vertices (3-4 keys or indices), uv?, texture?}], origin?, rotation?, parent?, texture?} (faces without uv get Blockbench's Auto UV); add_mesh_primitive {shape: cuboid|beveled_cuboid|pyramid|plane|circle|cylinder|tube|cone|sphere|icosphere|octahedron|dodecahedron|torus, diameter?, height?, sides?, align_edges?, detail?, minor_diameter?, minor_sides?, edge_size?, name?, origin?, rotation?, parent?, texture?} (Blockbench's Add Mesh dialog, same geometry and UVs); edit_mesh {target, actions: [set_vertices {vertices} | move_vertices {keys?, offset} | delete_vertices {keys} | transform {keys?, translate?, rotate?, scale?, pivot?} | add_faces {faces} | delete_faces {faces} | flip_faces {faces?} | merge_vertices {distance?, keys?, in_center?} | extrude_faces {faces, distance, direction?, even_extend?} | subdivide {faces?, cuts?} | loop_cut {face, direction?, cuts?, offset?, spacing?}]} (applied in order); map_mesh_uv {target, faces?, mode: auto|project_x|project_y|project_z|explicit, uv?, scale?, texture?}. Meshes are only allowed in the free (Generic) format. Nodes, textures and animations are addressed by UUID or exact name. Coordinates are absolute model units; rotations are degrees applied Z·Y·X about the origin. Format rules: a batch is refused when the nodes it adds or changes break the model format's limits, the way Blockbench would (meshes only in the free format; java_block cubes within -16..32 with rotations the model's java_block_version allows; no group rotation in java_block; box UV and integer sizes where forced). Softer problems come back as format_warnings.

tools.name: mcp__bbmodel__bbmodel_export_bedrock_geometry
tools.description: Compiles a .bbmodel to Minecraft Bedrock geometry (.geo.json) using the same conventions as Blockbench's Bedrock codec: mirrored X, flipped up/down UVs, bb_main for root cubes, and visible bounds. Only cubes are exported; other element types are listed in skipped. Returns the JSON inline when no output path is given.

file.description: Path to a .bbmodel file, absolute or relative to the first workspace root.

output.description: Output .json path inside the workspace; omit to return the geometry inline.

identifier.description: Geometry identifier; defaults to the model identifier or name.

tools.name: mcp__bbmodel__bbmodel_export_java_block
tools.description: Compiles a .bbmodel to a Minecraft Java Edition block/item model .json the way Blockbench's Java Block/Item codec does: format_version, textures map (#id → namespace:folder/name), elements with 16-scale UVs, rotation (single-axis angle/axis for older versions, x/y/z for 1.21.11+ and 26.3), cullface, tintindex, display, groups and ambientocclusion. Meshes and other non-cube elements are skipped and listed in notes. Returns the JSON inline when no output path is given.

file.description: Path to a .bbmodel file, absolute or relative to the first workspace root.

output.description: Output .json path inside the workspace (usually assets/<namespace>/models/block/<name>.json); omit to return the model inline.

version.description: Target java_block_version; defaults to the model's own, then 26.3.

export_groups.description: Write Blockbench's groups outliner export (default true, like Blockbench).

export_pivots.description: Write zero-angle rotation blocks for cubes with a pivot (Blockbench's java_export_pivots, default true).

tools.name: mcp__bbmodel__bbmodel_info
tools.description: Summarizes a .bbmodel file: format, version, resolution, node counts, world-space bounds and the current revision. Start here before editing.

file.description: Path to a .bbmodel file, absolute or relative to the first workspace root.

tools.name: mcp__bbmodel__bbmodel_render
tools.description: Renders a .bbmodel file to a PNG with bb-render (headless three.js WebGPU), without Blockbench. Returns the image and its path. Optionally poses the model at a time in an animation clip. Views are relative to the model's front (-Z). The first render on a machine downloads and installs the render engine's packages with npm (three, three-blockbench and Dawn, about 130 MB) into a per-user cache folder; later renders reuse them.

file.description: Path to a .bbmodel file, absolute or relative to the first workspace root.

preset.description: bb-render preset; icon is orthographic with a transparent background.

output.description: PNG path inside the workspace; defaults to a scratch file outside it.

overwrite.description: Allow output to replace an existing PNG.

clip.description: Animation clip name or index; renders the pose at time.

tools.name: mcp__bbmodel__bbmodel_validate
tools.description: Runs geometry gates on a .bbmodel file in its rest pose and reports every violation by node name. Gates: outliner (broken references, duplicate UUIDs), unlisted_nodes, degenerate (slivers, inverted cubes), block_limits (Java or Bedrock block size), floating (parts touching nothing in the main body), interpenetration (deep overlaps across groups), mirror (left/right parts that are not mirror images). self_test plants each gate's defect into a copy and confirms the gate catches it; a gate that does not discriminate on this model should not be trusted. GeckoLib rules run automatically for geckolib_model files.

file.description: Path to a .bbmodel file, absolute or relative to the first workspace root.

block_limits.description: Defaults to java_block for java_block models, bedrock_block for bedrock_block models, otherwise none.

free_elements.description: Element names allowed to float (deliberately detached parts).

asymmetric.description: Group or element names excluded from the mirror gate.

mirror_x.description: X of the symmetry plane; defaults to 8 for java_block and 0 otherwise.

material_key.description: Exempt overlapping parts that share this material key.

geckolib.description: Force GeckoLib rules on or off.

tools.name: mcp__bbmodel__blockbench_launch
tools.description: Starts the Blockbench desktop app, optionally opening a file from the workspace (.bbmodel, .json, .obj, .gltf, .glb or .png). If Blockbench is already running, the file opens as a new tab in that window. Set wait_for_mcp_ms to wait until the desktop Blockbench MCP plugin answers, before driving the app with that server. The app is found from --blockbench, $BLOCKBENCH_PATH, blockbench on PATH, or the standard install folders. On Linux it needs a display, and snap or flatpak builds may be unable to read folders outside your home.

file.description: File to open, absolute or relative to the first workspace root.

wait_for_mcp_ms.description: Wait up to this long for the desktop plugin's MCP endpoint to answer; 0 returns right after launching.

tools.name: mcp__blockbench__capture_app_screenshot
tools.description: Returns the image data of the Blockbench app.

max_size.description: Longest side of the returned image in pixels; larger images are scaled down proportionally. Omit for full size.

format.description: Encoding of the returned image: "png" (default, lossless), or the smaller "jpeg" (no transparency: transparent pixels become white) or "webp".

tools.name: mcp__blockbench__capture_screenshot
tools.description: Returns the rendered image of a view. Defaults to the user's active viewport ("active"); pass the ID of an offscreen view from create_offscreen_view to render without disturbing the user, or a viewport ID from list_views.

view.description: View to target: "active" for the viewport the user last interacted with, the ID of an offscreen view from create_offscreen_view, or a viewport ID from list_views.

max_size.description: Longest side of the returned image in pixels; larger images are scaled down proportionally. Omit for full size.

format.description: Encoding of the returned image: "png" (default, lossless), or the smaller "jpeg" (no transparency: transparent pixels become white) or "webp".

tools.name: mcp__blockbench__geckolib_export_animations
tools.description: Compiles the project's animations into GeckoLib animation-file JSON, including the easing and easingArgs the plugin writes, and optionally writes it to a path. The text is formatted like Blockbench's own export (its JSON indentation, minify and final-newline settings). Reports which host API compiled it, since only the plugin-patched route stamps geckolib_format_version. Set mode='dialog' to trigger the plugin's own animation export action instead.

mode.description: compile returns the file content without touching the UI. dialog triggers the GeckoLib plugin's own export action, which opens a native save dialog for the user to complete and updates the project's cached export path.

path.description: Absolute filesystem path to write the compiled content to. Requires Blockbench filesystem permission. Only used in compile mode. Fails if the file exists unless overwrite is true.

overwrite.description: Replace an existing file at path. Defaults to false so a re-export never silently replaces a reference file.

max_content_length.description: Maximum characters of content to return. Use 0 to omit the content and only report its size.

animation_ids.description: Animation UUIDs or names to include. Omit to export every animation in the project.

tools.name: mcp__blockbench__geckolib_validate_model
tools.description: Checks the GeckoLib project against rules derived from the plugin and the GeckoLib runtime: bone-name charset and duplicates, mod ID and object ID validity, armor template bones, texture size against the UV base, and (optionally) compiled animation loop values, easing names, easing arguments and lengths. Each finding carries a stable check ID. Passing does not prove in-game correctness.

include_animations.description: Also compile the project's animations and validate their loop values, easings and lengths.

tools.name: mcp__blockbench__risky_eval
tools.description: Evaluates JavaScript and returns its JSON result. Does not create an Undo entry. Mutating code must manage its own correctly scoped Undo transaction; read-only evaluation leaves history unchanged.

code.description: JavaScript code to evaluate. Do not pass `console` commands or comments.

tools.name: DeferredToolPlaceholder

tools.name: mcp__blockbench__set_camera_angle
tools.description: Moves a view's camera and returns the resulting frame plus the applied camera state. Defaults to the user's active viewport, which changes what they see and clears any side-view lock they had; target an offscreen view from create_offscreen_view to inspect the model from any angle without moving their camera.

This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

<tools-used-before-summary>Agent, AskUserQuestion, Bash, Edit, ExitPlanMode, Grep, Read, ToolSearch, WebSearch, Write, mcp__bbmodel__bbmodel_render, mcp__bbmodel__blockbench_launch, mcp__blockbench__capture_app_screenshot, mcp__blockbench__risky_eval, mcp__blockbench__set_camera_angle</tools-used-before-summary>
Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent:
   - **Item models.** The user added Blockbench (MCP + studio) and wanted 3D models for the mod's items, with design references from magic/RPG mods. Chosen scope: "Físicos clave". Chosen style: dark arcane fantasy (leather, brass, gems; matches DESIGN.md).
   - **Plugins and in-game check.** The user listed the installed Blockbench plugins (GeckoLib Models & Animations, Bone View, Animation Sliders, Animation to JSON Converter, Free Rotation, MCP Server). The new models did not show in game; the cause was stale build resources.
   - **Rest of the items and generic weapons.** "Crear modelos para el resto de objetos del mod y genericos para asignar a las armas".
   - **Mobs.** "Hacen falta modelos para los mobs y enemigos". User choices: GeckoLib + own entities; about 12–15 reusable archetypes.
   - The user rejected the first mob plan, asking: "Validar contra mods populares de criaturas, estrategias utilizadas para manejo de multiples modelos y diseños y considerar usar arte de licencia libre". The revised plan was approved. Its art policy: CC0, or CC-BY with credit; no copying other mods' art; original procedural art.
   - **Latest request** (with a screenshot of the dragons in game): "se ve bien, optimizar variantes y colores para no generar un modelo para cada una de ellas".

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - Minecraft 1.20.1, Forge 47.4.22, Parchment mappings, Java 17.
   - The mod has a single item, `dndsheets:token`. Each look (`ItemLook`) is a `CustomModelData` value of `ordinal()+1`; the enum is append-only.
   - Weapons are vanilla items carrying a `customModelData` from `weapons.json`. The overrides live in `assets/minecraft/models/item/<base>.json`.
   - GeckoLib 4.4.9 (cloudsmith maven), now a hard dependency, `[4.4,5)`.
   - One generic entity, `dndsheets:monster_model` (`MonsterModelEntity`), with synced `model`/`variant`/flying/baby data.
   - Monsters opt in with `baseEntity: "dndsheets:monster_model"` plus `appearance.model` and `appearance.variant`. A skin pack for another creature mod (`MonsterSkins` / `reskin`) still wins because it replaces `baseEntity`.
   - Each archetype ships one `mask.png` plus `variants.json` (palettes). The client colours the mask into a cached `DynamicTexture` per variant. `appearance.variant` may also be `"#RRGGBB"`, from which a palette is derived.
   - Mask encoding: R = mix toward dark, G = role×40 (roles: base, dark, belly, horn, membrane, eye), B = whiten, A = 255 painted.
   - Pipeline: the headless bbmodel MCP is driven through `tools/blockbench/bbmcp.py` (`Client().call(tool, args)`).
     - Its workspace root is `tools/blockbench`, so exports must go inside it and are then copied into the assets.
     - Box-UV shelf packing is done by the script, with a procedural painter.
     - Format is `geckolib_model`, exported with `bbmodel_export_bedrock_geometry` (format 1.12.0).
   - Animation JSON uses plain keys `idle fly attack hurt death`.
   - Wyrmlings keep `appearance.baby: true`, rendered at half size via `scaleModelForRender` and `getDimensions` scaled 0.5.

3. Files and Code Sections:

   **Item models (done earlier)**
   - `tools/blockbench/build_items.py`
     - Builds `dm_wand`, `move_wand`, `rest_kit`, `summon_card`, `summon_card_filled` with a swatch palette.
     - Defines `GENERATED_DISPLAY`, `pal()`, `palette()`, `rgb()`.
   - `tools/blockbench/build_more.py`
     - 16 ability medallions (glyph bitmaps).
     - 21 weapon models in `models/item/weapon/<id>.json`, sharing the texture `weapon_3d.png`. Their `customModelData` values are 1001–1021.
   - `src/main/resources/dndsheets/defaults/weapons.json`: `customModelData` added to those 21 weapons.
   - `assets/minecraft/models/item/*.json`: 16 vanilla override files. `stick` (used by flail) uses `handheld_rod`.
   - `tools/generate_item_icons.py`: `HAND_AUTHORED = set(LOOKS)`, so it no longer overwrites any look.
   - Weapons with a trident or fishing_rod base (javelin, spear, pike, trident, whip) were skipped.

   **GeckoLib setup**
   - `build.gradle`:
     - Repo: `maven { url = "https://dl.cloudsmith.io/public/geckolib3/geckolib/maven/"; content { includeGroup "software.bernie.geckolib" } }`
     - Dependency: `implementation fg.deobf("software.bernie.geckolib:geckolib-forge-1.20.1:4.4.9")`
   - `src/main/resources/META-INF/mods.toml`: geckolib dependency block placed after the pehkui block (mandatory, `[4.4,5)`, AFTER, BOTH).

   **Entity and rendering**
   - `src/main/java/net/hawthorn/dndsheets/entity/MonsterModelEntity.java` (new)
     - Extends `PathfinderMob`, implements `GeoEntity`.
     - Synced `MODEL`, `VARIANT`, `FLYING`, `BABY`. Defaults: `"dragon"` / `"red"`.
     - `configure(model, variant, flying)`; overrides `isBaby`/`setBaby` (calls `refreshDimensions`) and `getDimensions` (×0.5 for baby).
     - NBT keys: `Model`, `Variant`, `FlyingPose`, `Baby`.
     - Static `play(Entity, trigger)` calls `triggerAnim("action", trigger)` on the server; `hurt()` triggers `"hurt"`.
     - Controllers:
       - `"main"`: `death` (`thenPlayAndHold`), else `fly` or `idle` (`thenLoop`).
       - `"action"`: triggerable `attack` and `hurt`.
     - `createAttributes()`: max health 20, speed 0.25.
   - `src/main/java/net/hawthorn/dndsheets/init/DndsheetsModEntities.java` (new)
     - DeferredRegister `MONSTER_MODEL`: `MobCategory.MISC`, sized 1×1, tracking range 10.
     - `registerAttributes(EntityAttributeCreationEvent)`.
   - `DndsheetsMod.java`: registers `DndsheetsModEntities.REGISTRY` and adds the `registerAttributes` listener.
   - `src/main/java/net/hawthorn/dndsheets/client/MonsterModelRenderer.java` (new)
     - `@Mod.EventBusSubscriber(bus = MOD, value = CLIENT)`; extends `GeoEntityRenderer`; shadow 0.6.
     - `getDeathMaxRotation` returns 0.
     - `scaleModelForRender` multiplies width and height by 0.5 when the entity is a baby.
     - `reloadTextures(RegisterClientReloadListenersEvent)` registers a `ResourceManagerReloadListener` that calls `MonsterTextures.clear()`.
     - Registers the renderer.
     - Inner `Model extends GeoModel`, with a ResourceLocation cache:
       - `geo/entity/<model>.geo.json`
       - `animations/entity/<model>.animation.json`
       - texture from `MonsterTextures.get(model, variant)`
   - `src/main/java/net/hawthorn/dndsheets/client/MonsterTextures.java` (new, latest work)
     - `get(model, variant)` caches the result of `build()`.
     - `build()`:
       - reads the palette;
       - opens `textures/entity/<model>/mask.png` as a `NativeImage`;
       - colours each pixel with `colour(abgr, palette)`;
       - registers a `DynamicTexture` at `dndsheets:dynamic/<model>/<sanitized variant>`.
       - On any exception it logs a warning and returns `MissingTextureAtlasSprite.getLocation()`.
     - `palette()`: a `#hex` variant calls `derived()`; otherwise it reads `variants.json` and falls back to the first key.
     - `clear()` releases the cached textures.
     - The unused `JsonElement` import and the `mix(float, …)` overload were removed.

   **Monster data and registry**
   - `MonsterRegistry.java`
     - `Appearance` record gained `String model, String variant`; `DEFAULT` and `GLOWING` are updated; `isDefault` checks both new fields.
     - `parseAppearance` reads `model` and `variant`; `writeAppearance` writes them.
     - `applyLooks` calls `own.configure(look.model, look.variant, block.flies())` before the early return.
     - The baby branch now also handles `MonsterModelEntity own` with `own.setBaby(true)`.
   - `monsters.json`: 40 color dragons (wyrmling, young, adult, ancient) moved to `baseEntity` `dndsheets:monster_model` with `appearance {model: "dragon", variant: <color>}`. Wyrmlings keep `"baby": true`.

   **Tests**
   - `src/test/java/net/hawthorn/dndsheets/JsonContentSelfTest.java`:
     - The appearance key set now includes `model` and `variant`.
     - The namespace and vanilla-item checks skip `model` and `variant`.
     - New check: a monster that names a model must have `baseEntity` `monster_model`, and must ship the geo, animation, `mask.png` and `variants.json`.
     - New check: the variant is a key of `variants.json` or starts with `#`.
   - `gametest/CombatantGameTests.java`: added `aShippedDragonWearsItsOwnModel`. It covers spawn, model/variant, baby, `Combatant`, and the NBT round trip. It has not been run (see Problem Solving).

   **Mob tooling and assets**
   - `tools/blockbench/mobs/mobkit.py` (rewritten in the latest step)
     - `Cube`, `pack`, `pixels()` (returns role / dark / whiten per pixel), `mask_png`, `preview_png`.
     - `Archetype.build` writes the bbmodel with a preview texture of the first palette, then exports the geo to `tools/blockbench/out` and copies it into the assets.
     - `install_textures` deletes old PNGs, writes `mask.png`, and writes `variants.json` as `{variant: {role: [r, g, b]}}`.
     - `install_animations` and the `keys()` helper.
   - `tools/blockbench/mobs/dragon.py`
     - 15 bones (root, body, neck1/2, head, jaw, tail1–3, wing_l/r, four legs) and 51 cubes.
     - `pair()` mirrors left/right cubes onto a shared UV.
     - 10 palettes: red, blue, green, black, white, brass, bronze, copper, gold, silver.
     - Animations: idle, fly, attack, hurt, death.
   - Assets:
     - `assets/dndsheets/geo/entity/dragon.geo.json`
     - `assets/dndsheets/animations/entity/dragon.animation.json`
     - `assets/dndsheets/textures/entity/dragon/mask.png`
     - `assets/dndsheets/textures/entity/dragon/variants.json` (the 10 per-colour PNGs were removed)

   **Docs**
   - `CREDITS.md`: creature models section and the licence policy.
   - `CHANGELOG.md`: "Unreleased" entry.
   - `PROJECT_CONTEXT.md`:
     - Removed "own creature models" from the out-of-scope lines.
     - Added an "Own creature models (GeckoLib)" section, now updated to describe the mask + `variants.json` design and "Done and seen in game: dragon".

4. Errors and fixes:
   - **Headless renders blank.** All bbmodel renders were white, and so was the desktop Blockbench viewport (WebGL issue on this machine). Verification relied on validate, the build, and the user checking in game.
   - **Item models not showing in game.** The `build/resources` output was stale; running `./gradlew processResources` fixed it.
   - **Bash heredoc failures.** A heredoc with nested quoting failed with "unexpected EOF". Java files were then written with the Write tool, and edits went through scratchpad Python scripts.
   - **Broken patch in `mobkit.py`.** A `'\n'` escape inside a patch broke the file; fixed with `chr(10)`.
   - **Export outside the workspace.** The bbmodel export refused paths outside its root; now exports to `tools/blockbench/out` and copies the file.
   - **Self-test failures.**
     - `model` was treated as an item id; fixed by skipping `model` and `variant`.
     - "a dragon wyrmling should come out as a baby": baby was restored for wyrmlings and implemented on the entity.
   - **`runGameTestServer` fails** in dev because the mods required by the existing hard dependencies (Patchouli, Jade, Curios, Pehkui, Origins) are missing. This was already the case and has nothing to do with GeckoLib.
   - **First mob plan rejected** by the user, who asked for validation against popular creature mods and consideration of free-licence art. The plan was revised with research on Ice and Fire variants, GeckoLib `getTextureLocation` variants, licences, and CC0 Quaternius / OpenGameArt packs.

5. Problem Solving:
   - `./gradlew build` passes with all checks, including `testJsonContent`, `checkPortabilityCoupling` and `checkAssetCredits`, after the mask/palette change.
   - The user confirmed the dragons render well in game.

6. All user messages:
   - "Se ha agregado la opción de trabajar con blockbench a traves de mcp y studio, se desea agregar modelos para los objetos del mod, buscar estilos y diseños existentes en mods de magia y rpg para obtener buenos diseños para objetos e items"
   - Answers: scope "Físicos clave (Recommended)", style "Fantasía arcana oscura (Recommended)"; plan approved.
   - "No aplicados, plugins disponibles: GeckoLib Models and animations, one view, animation slider, animation to JSON converter, free rotation y MCP server"
   - Clarification answer: "Los modelos no se ven en el juego".
   - "Crear modelos par ael resto de objetos del mod y genericos para asignar a las armas"
   - "Hacen falta modelos para los mobs y enemigos"
   - Answers: "GeckoLib + entidades propias (Recommended)", "Arquetipos clave ~12-15 (Recommended)".
   - Plan rejection: "Validar contra mods populares de criaturas, estrategias utilizadas para manejo de multiples modelos y diseños y considerar usar arte de licencia libre". The revised plan was then approved.
   - "[Image #1] se ve bien, optimizar variantes y colores para no generar un modelo para cada una de ellas"

7. Pending Tasks:
   - The remaining 13 archetypes from the approved plan: goblinoid, brute, reptilian, demon, ooze, spider, beast, golem, elemental, bird, humanoid, undead, aquatic. Each is one mask, a palettes file, and a `monsters.json` mapping.
   - Hook `MonsterModelEntity.play(entity, "attack")` into `MonsterActionManager` and `CombatManager`.
   - Phase 0 licence audit (LICENSE files of the reference mods); `reference/` notes.
   - Fly animation is unused, because the dragons have no `flies` flag.

8. Current Work:
   I had just finished the variant optimization. Variants went from one PNG per colour to a single `mask.png` plus `variants.json` per archetype, coloured client-side by `MonsterTextures` into cached `DynamicTexture`s, with `#RRGGBB` variant support and cache clearing on resource reload. `mobkit.py`, the renderer, the self-test and `PROJECT_CONTEXT.md` were updated, and `dragon.py` was re-run. `./gradlew build` succeeded; the jar shrank from about 2.07 MB to 2.02 MB. The user had not yet been told the result.

9. Optional Next Step:
   - Report to the user, in Spanish, that the variant optimization is done:
     - one mask plus `variants.json`, coloured on the client;
     - a new colour is one JSON line, or a `"#RRGGBB"` value in `monsters.json`;
     - the build passes.
   - Ask the user to rerun `./gradlew runClient` and confirm the colours look the same as before.

Ya no hay un PNG por color: cada arquetipo tiene una máscara y un `variants.json`, y el cliente pinta cada variante al usarla por primera vez. El `./gradlew build` pasa con el self-test actualizado, pero no he vuelto a abrir el juego, así que el recoloreado en pantalla está sin verificar.

**Cómo funciona ahora**
- **Máscara:** `textures/entity/dragon/mask.png` no guarda colores. Cada píxel guarda su rol (base, sombra, vientre, cuerno, membrana u ojo), cuánta sombra mezclar y un brillo.

**Qué cambia en la práctica**
- **Colores y hex:** un color nuevo es una entrada en `variants.json`. `appearance.variant` también acepta un hex directo como `"#2a9d8f"`, y de ese color se derivan las demás tonalidades.
- **Archivos por arquetipo:** pasa de 10 PNG a 2 archivos (`mask.png` y `variants.json`), sin importar cuántos colores tenga. Los otros 13 arquetipos seguirán el mismo esquema.
- **Self-test:** comprueba que exista la máscara y que cada `variant` esté en `variants.json` o sea un hex.
- **Un solo modelo:** ya lo era. Las 10 variantes de color y las 4 edades (cría, joven, adulto, antiguo) comparten el mismo modelo, y la edad se resuelve por escala.

Un hex inválido o una máscara que falte dibujan la textura de "missing", con un aviso en el log, en vez de romper el render. El script `dragon.py` regenera todo con `python tools/blockbench/mobs/dragon.py`.

Cuando confirmes que los colores se ven igual que antes en `runClient`, sigo con los siguientes arquetipos (goblinoide, bruto, reptiliano, etc.) con este mismo esquema. entries.name: ExitPlanMode
entries.description:
Use this tool when you are in plan mode and have finished writing your plan to the plan file and are ready for user approval.

## How This Tool Works
- You should have already written your plan to the plan file specified in the plan mode system message
- This tool does NOT take the plan content as a parameter - it will read the plan from the file you wrote
- This tool simply signals that you're done planning and ready for the user to review and approve
- The user will see the contents of your plan file when they review it

## When to Use This Tool
IMPORTANT: Only use this tool when the task requires planning the implementation steps of a task that requires writing code. For research tasks where you're gathering information, searching files, reading files or in general trying to understand the codebase - do NOT use this tool.

## Before Using This Tool
Ensure your plan is complete and unambiguous:
- If you have unresolved questions about requirements or approach, use AskUserQuestion first (in earlier phases)
- Once your plan is finalized, use THIS tool to request approval

**Important:** Do NOT use AskUserQuestion to ask "Is this plan okay?" or "Should I proceed?" - that's exactly what THIS tool does. ExitPlanMode inherently requests user approval of your plan.

## Examples

1. Initial task: "Search for and understand the implementation of vim mode in the codebase" - Do not use the exit plan mode tool because you are not planning the implementation steps of a task.
2. Initial task: "Help me implement yank mode for vim" - Use the exit plan mode tool after you have finished planning the implementation steps of the task.
3. Initial task: "Add a new feature to handle user authentication" - If unsure about auth method (OAuth, JWT, etc.), use AskUserQuestion first, then use exit plan mode tool after clarifying the approach.

entries.name: mcp__bbmodel__bbmodel_add_texture
entries.description: Embeds a PNG into a .bbmodel file as a new texture, from a PNG file inside the workspace or a PNG data URL. Optionally puts it in a PBR material channel (create the material first with bbmodel_edit add_material) and assigns it to every face of some cubes or groups. Assign only color textures to faces; normal, height and MER textures reach the faces through their material.

expected_revision.description: Revision from an earlier read. The write is refused if another agent changed the file since then.

name.description: Defaults to the PNG file name.

material.description: PBR material (UUID or name) to put the texture in.

channel.description: Channel inside the material: color, normal, height or mer (R metal, G emissive, B roughness). Defaults to color.

wrap_mode.description: repeat tiles the image on faces whose UVs exceed it.

render_mode.description: emissive makes the texture glow (signs, light panels).

assign_to.description: Cubes or groups (UUID or name) whose faces should use the texture.

entries.name: mcp__bbmodel__bbmodel_create
entries.description: Creates a new, empty .bbmodel file (format 5.0). Build it up with bbmodel_edit. Refuses to replace an existing file unless overwrite is true.

file.description: Path to a .bbmodel file, absolute or relative to the first workspace root.

format.description: Blockbench format ID: free, bedrock, bedrock_block, java_block, geckolib_model, modded_entity, ...

box_uv.description: Defaults to true for entity formats (bedrock, geckolib_model, modded_entity, ...) and false otherwise.

entries.name: mcp__bbmodel__bbmodel_edit
entries.description: Applies edit operations to a .bbmodel file in order, as one atomic write. If any operation fails, nothing is written and the error names the failing operation. Operations (field op): add_group {name, origin, rotation, parent}; add_cube {name, from, to, origin?, rotation?, inflate?, parent?, box_uv?, uv_offset?, mirror_uv?, texture?, faces?} (box-UV faces are laid out automatically); update_node {target, name?, origin?, rotation?, from?, to?, inflate?, uv_offset?, mirror_uv?, faces?, parent?} (parent moves the node; box UV is recomputed); remove_node {target} (groups are removed with their contents and animators); add_texture {name, source: PNG data URL, width, height, material?, channel?, wrap_mode?, render_mode?} (bbmodel_add_texture reads a PNG file for you); add_material {name, color_value?, mer_value?, subsurface_value?} (a PBR material; its textures fill the color, normal or height, and mer channels); update_material {target, name?, color_value?, mer_value?, subsurface_value?}; update_texture {target, name?, source?, width?, height?, material?, channel?, wrap_mode?, render_mode?} (material null removes it from its material); assign_texture {targets, texture, faces?, mesh_faces?} (cubes and meshes); add_animation {name, length, loop, snapping}; remove_animation {animation}; set_keyframe {animation, bone, channel, time, value, interpolation} (replaces a key at the same channel and time); remove_keyframe {animation, bone, channel, time}; set_model_properties {name?, model_identifier?, resolution?}; add_locator {name, parent?, position, rotation?, ignore_inherited_scale?} (a named point particle effects spawn at; position is absolute model units); set_particle_keyframe {animation, time, effect, file?, locator?, pre_effect_script?, bind_to_actor?} (file is the particle JSON path relative to the .bbmodel, from bbmodel_particle_effect; replaces the same effect at the same time); remove_particle_keyframe {animation, time, effect?}; add_mesh {name, vertices (key map or [x,y,z] list, relative to origin), faces [{vertices (3-4 keys or indices), uv?, texture?}], origin?, rotation?, parent?, texture?} (faces without uv get Blockbench's Auto UV); add_mesh_primitive {shape: cuboid|beveled_cuboid|pyramid|plane|circle|cylinder|tube|cone|sphere|icosphere|octahedron|dodecahedron|torus, diameter?, height?, sides?, align_edges?, detail?, minor_diameter?, minor_sides?, edge_size?, name?, origin?, rotation?, parent?, texture?} (Blockbench's Add Mesh dialog, same geometry and UVs); edit_mesh {target, actions: [set_vertices {vertices} | move_vertices {keys?, offset} | delete_vertices {keys} | transform {keys?, translate?, rotate?, scale?, pivot?} | add_faces {faces} | delete_faces {faces} | flip_faces {faces?} | merge_vertices {distance?, keys?, in_center?} | extrude_faces {faces, distance, direction?, even_extend?} | subdivide {faces?, cuts?} | loop_cut {face, direction?, cuts?, offset?, spacing?}]} (applied in order); map_mesh_uv {target, faces?, mode: auto|project_x|project_y|project_z|explicit, uv?, scale?, texture?}. Meshes are only allowed in the free (Generic) format. Nodes, textures and animations are addressed by UUID or exact name. Coordinates are absolute model units; rotations are degrees applied Z·Y·X about the origin. Format rules: a batch is refused when the nodes it adds or changes break the model format's limits, the way Blockbench would (meshes only in the free format; java_block cubes within -16..32 with rotations the model's java_block_version allows; no group rotation in java_block; box UV and integer sizes where forced). Softer problems come back as format_warnings.

vertices.description: {key: [x, y, z]} keeping your keys, or an array of [x, y, z] (4-character keys are generated). Positions are relative to origin.
3 or 4 distinct vertices, by key or by index (index into the vertex list/array; for edit_mesh, into the mesh's current vertex keys in saved order). Blockbench meshes do not support n-gons.

Texture for every face that does not name one.

Vertices to transform; omit for all.

entries.name: mcp__bbmodel__bbmodel_export_bedrock_geometry
entries.description: Compiles a .bbmodel to Minecraft Bedrock geometry (.geo.json) using the same conventions as Blockbench's Bedrock codec: mirrored X, flipped up/down UVs, bb_main for root cubes, and visible bounds. Only cubes are exported; other element types are listed in skipped. Returns the JSON inline when no output path is given.

file.description: Path to a .bbmodel file, absolute or relative to the first workspace root.

output.description: Output .json path inside the workspace; omit to return the geometry inline.

identifier.description: Geometry identifier; defaults to the model identifier or name.

entries.name: mcp__bbmodel__bbmodel_export_java_block
entries.description: Compiles a .bbmodel to a Minecraft Java Edition block/item model .json the way Blockbench's Java Block/Item codec does: format_version, textures map (#id → namespace:folder/name), elements with 16-scale UVs, rotation (single-axis angle/axis for older versions, x/y/z for 1.21.11+ and 26.3), cullface, tintindex, display, groups and ambientocclusion. Meshes and other non-cube elements are skipped and listed in notes. Returns the JSON inline when no output path is given.

file.description: Path to a .bbmodel file, absolute or relative to the first workspace root.

output.description: Output .json path inside the workspace (usually assets/<namespace>/models/block/<name>.json); omit to return the model inline.

version.description: Target java_block_version; defaults to the model's own, then 26.3.

export_groups.description: Write Blockbench's groups outliner export (default true, like Blockbench).

export_pivots.description: Write zero-angle rotation blocks for cubes with a pivot (Blockbench's java_export_pivots, default true).

entries.name: mcp__bbmodel__bbmodel_info
entries.description: Summarizes a .bbmodel file: format, version, resolution, node counts, world-space bounds and the current revision. Start here before editing.

file.description: Path to a .bbmodel file, absolute or relative to the first workspace root.

entries.name: mcp__bbmodel__bbmodel_render
entries.description: Renders a .bbmodel file to a PNG with bb-render (headless three.js WebGPU), without Blockbench. Returns the image and its path. Optionally poses the model at a time in an animation clip. Views are relative to the model's front (-Z). The first render on a machine downloads and installs the render engine's packages with npm (three, three-blockbench and Dawn, about 130 MB) into a per-user cache folder; later renders reuse them.

file.description: Path to a .bbmodel file, absolute or relative to the first workspace root.

preset.description: bb-render preset; icon is orthographic with a transparent background.

output.description: PNG path inside the workspace; defaults to a scratch file outside it.

overwrite.description: Allow output to replace an existing PNG.

clip.description: Animation clip name or index; renders the pose at time.

entries.name: mcp__bbmodel__bbmodel_validate
entries.description: Runs geometry gates on a .bbmodel file in its rest pose and reports every violation by node name. Gates: outliner (broken references, duplicate UUIDs), unlisted_nodes, degenerate (slivers, inverted cubes), block_limits (Java or Bedrock block size), floating (parts touching nothing in the main body), interpenetration (deep overlaps across groups), mirror (left/right parts that are not mirror images). self_test plants each gate's defect into a copy and confirms the gate catches it; a gate that does not discriminate on this model should not be trusted. GeckoLib rules run automatically for geckolib_model files.

file.description: Path to a .bbmodel file, absolute or relative to the first workspace root.

block_limits.description: Defaults to java_block for java_block models, bedrock_block for bedrock_block models, otherwise none.

free_elements.description: Element names allowed to float (deliberately detached parts).

asymmetric.description: Group or element names excluded from the mirror gate.

mirror_x.description: X of the symmetry plane; defaults to 8 for java_block and 0 otherwise.

material_key.description: Exempt overlapping parts that share this material key.

geckolib.description: Force GeckoLib rules on or off.

entries.name: mcp__bbmodel__blockbench_launch
entries.description: Starts the Blockbench desktop app, optionally opening a file from the workspace (.bbmodel, .json, .obj, .gltf, .glb or .png). If Blockbench is already running, the file opens as a new tab in that window. Set wait_for_mcp_ms to wait until the desktop Blockbench MCP plugin answers, before driving the app with that server. The app is found from --blockbench, $BLOCKBENCH_PATH, blockbench on PATH, or the standard install folders. On Linux it needs a display, and snap or flatpak builds may be unable to read folders outside your home.

file.description: File to open, absolute or relative to the first workspace root.

wait_for_mcp_ms.description: Wait up to this long for the desktop plugin's MCP endpoint to answer; 0 returns right after launching.

entries.name: mcp__blockbench__geckolib_export_animations
entries.description: Compiles the project's animations into GeckoLib animation-file JSON, including the easing and easingArgs the plugin writes, and optionally writes it to a path. The text is formatted like Blockbench's own export (its JSON indentation, minify and final-newline settings). Reports which host API compiled it, since only the plugin-patched route stamps geckolib_format_version. Set mode='dialog' to trigger the plugin's own animation export action instead.

mode.description: compile returns the file content without touching the UI. dialog triggers the GeckoLib plugin's own export action, which opens a native save dialog for the user to complete and updates the project's cached export path.

entries.name: mcp__blockbench__geckolib_validate_model
entries.description: Checks the GeckoLib project against rules derived from the plugin and the GeckoLib runtime: bone-name charset and duplicates, mod ID and object ID validity, armor template bones, texture size against the UV base, and (optionally) compiled animation loop values, easing names, easing arguments and lengths. Each finding carries a stable check ID. Passing does not prove in-game correctness.

include_animations.description: Also compile the project's animations and validate their loop values, easings and lengths.

Defaults to the user's active viewport, which changes what they see and clears any side-view lock they had; target an offscreen view from create_offscreen_view to inspect the model from any angle without moving their camera.

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

**Do not spawn agents unless the user asks.** Each spawn starts cold and re-derives context you already have — it's the expensive path on this plan. A task with "multiple angles," "thorough," or several parts is not a request to spawn; handle it inline with your own tools. Only use this tool when the user explicitly says to use a subagent, or names one of the available agent types.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

A fork runs in the background and keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate. Subagents run in the background; you'll be notified when one completes. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
